title: CMRS Begins Safety Inspection Of 14.6 Km Chennai Metro Phase II Stretch
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Feb 12, 2026 | Updated 10:30 AM GMT+5:30

Chennai Metro Rail’s Phase II has moved a step closer to partial operations, with the Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety (CMRS) commencing mandatory statutory inspections on a priority elevated stretch of Corridor 4.
The two-day inspection, led by Anant Madhukar Chowdhary of the Bengaluru Circle, began on Wednesday and covers the 14.64 km elevated segment between Poonamallee Bypass and Vadapalani.
This section comprises 11 stations and forms part of one of the most anticipated corridors under Phase II.
On the opening day, the CMRS team examined a 6.13 km portion between Poonamallee Bypass and Iyyapanthangal.
Stations along this stretch include Poonamallee, Mullaithottam, Karayanchavadi, Kumananchavadi, Kattupakkam and Iyyapanthangal.
Officials said the inspection focused on core safety and operational parameters such as structural stability, track geometry, signalling interfaces and electrical systems.
Senior officials from Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL), including director (projects) T Archunan and director (systems and operations) Manoj Goyal, were present during the review, along with deputy CMRS officers and technical teams.
Corridor 4, which will eventually connect Light House in central Chennai to Poonamallee on the city’s western edge, is expected to significantly ease congestion along major arterial routes.
The decision to prioritise operations up to Vadapalani, earlier targeted for a later launch, was taken in view of projected ridership demand and commuter pressure in the western suburbs.
Once the CMRS grants approval, the proposal will move to the Railway Board for formal authorisation. Following that clearance, both the Union and Tamil Nadu governments will be notified before a final date for public operations is announced.
Arjun Brij is a Newsroom Associate at Swarajya. He tweets at @arjun_brij
